result.title: The Locality Trade-off in Masked Patch Self-Distillation
result.summary: Masked patch self-distillation is a key component of modern vision foundation models, including DINOv2 and DINOv3, yet its implications for local visual information remain unclear. We show that its semantic benefits can coexist with a scale-dependent locality cost. Using two annotation-free diagnostics, we distinguish recoverable local appearance from spatial correspondence. In smaller models, adding iBOT substantially weakens patch correspondence while largely preserving appearance decodability. In larger models, correspondence improves, but pixel and texture evidence becomes less linearly accessible in deep features. Thus, scaling changes the form of the locality cost rather than uniformly eliminating it. Our analysis of Gram anchoring further shows that preserving patch relations does not guarantee simultaneous improvements in both properties. These findings motivate evaluating and designing visual representations around the complementary demands of semantic abstraction, appearance preservation, and spatial correspondence. Our code is available at https://github.com/winci-ai/jea.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用两种免标注诊断区分「可解码的局部外观」与「空间对应」，考察 DINOv2/v3 中 iBOT 掩码 patch 自蒸馏的局部信息代价如何随模型规模改变，并检验 Gram anchoring 能否同时保住两类性质。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断视觉编码器深层特征里像素/纹理细节与 patch 对应的保留情况，与 LVR 关注的「视觉细节是否留在内部状态、是否发生信息坍缩」高度贴合，可供核查不同骨干对推理所需证据可及性的影响。
